messages:
emma: Heads-up — found a reproducible leak when cancelling async stream iterators in the Python SDK (SSE/chunked). Repro on uvloop + httpx: the socket remains open after you break out of an async for and call the stream's aclose().

emma: Minimal repro (simplified):
```python
stream = client.stream('/v1/generate', ... )
async for chunk in stream:
    if should_stop(chunk):
        await stream.aclose()  # we expect this to clean up the transport
        break
```

emma: After that the underlying connection stays ESTABLISHED and process shows lots of TIME_WAIT / socket fds. Happens reliably in our sample-app under load. Anyone seen this? :confused:

mike: yup, saw the same locally. Looks like __anext__ raising CancelledError doesn't trigger the generator finalizer the way we expect, so httpx.Response.close() isn't called. I have a tiny repro gist.

mike: gist: https://gist.github.com/mike/0a1b2c3d4e5f (contains repro server + client)

tanvi: workaround for now: wrap the iterator with an explicit context manager that calls aclose on exit. Ugly but effective:
```python
class StreamCtx:
    def __init__(self, it): self._it = it
    async def __aenter__(self): return self._it
    async def __aexit__(self, *tb): await self._it.aclose()

async with StreamCtx(client.stream(...)) as stream:
    async for c in stream:
        if should_stop(c): break
```

tanvi: but the real fix is: client.stream should return an object that supports async context manager semantics so cleanup is guaranteed even on CancelledError.

ryan: note: there's also a related auth/retry interaction. If token refresh happens while streaming (401 -> refresh -> reconnect), we sometimes end up with a duplicate "final" chunk appended to the reconnected stream. That makes deduping on consumer side hard.

emma: yes — observed that too. When the reconnect path replays the last prefix, the final chunk is replayed causing double output. Happens when the server sends the final chunk at the same time the agent triggers reauth.

mike: hypothesis: our reconnect code is merging buffers instead of treating the reconnect as a new stream boundary. We should emit a special sentinel or an "event: reconnect" so clients can decide.

tanvi: also typing nit: current SDK typing is AsyncIterator[bytes], but in practice we yield decoded event strings (json lines). Can we standardize on AsyncIterator[str] and provide bytes/raw option? Typing mismatch makes mypy noise in sample apps.

emma: agreed. For backwards compatibility, maybe keep raw_bytes param defaulting to False and update types: AsyncIterator[str] when raw_bytes is False, AsyncIterator[bytes] when True. Add overloads in stub file.

mike: plan proposal:
- short-term: add explicit Stream.aclose() docs + example with context manager wrapper in sample-apps repo
- medium-term: change stream object to be an async context manager + ensure __aexit__ always closes underlying response (even if CancelledError)
- long-term: revisit reconnect semantics for auth refresh to avoid final-chunk duplication (emit reconnect event)

ryan: +1. Also please add a regression test that uses uvloop/httpx combination in CI matrix — this only showed up there.

emma: I'll open an issue with repro steps and link the gist. tagging @mike to paste the exact stack.

mike: pasted stack (trimmed):
```
  File ".../py_sdk/stream.py", line 142, in __anext__
    chunk = await self._resp.aiter_text().__anext__()
  File "asyncio/tasks.py", line 350, in cancel
    raise CancelledError
  # underlying httpx Response remains open
```

mike: workaround that helped me in local dev: explicitly call `await stream._resp.aclose()` in cleanup, but obviously that's private and gross.

tanvi: can we also add an example showing how to integrate stream cancellation with FastAPI background tasks? People keep leaking fds when their request handler cancels early.

emma: yes — will add sample-app PR referencing the context manager wrapper + mypy-friendly typing changes.

ci-bot: created issue #3421 in github.com/redwood-inference/sdk: "py-sdk: async stream aclose edge cases + auth-reconnect duplication"

emma: thanks — will add a small failing CI test too. If someone from runtime team can review reconnect behavior (tanvi?) that would be great.

tanvi: happy to. I'll take a look at the reconnect buffer handling and see if we can emit a lightweight wire-level marker instead of replaying final chunk.

emma: perfect. tagging follow-ups: we should prioritize docs + sample-apps fix this sprint so users don't hit it in prod. :+1:
